To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the legal framework of CSR is not well established, but it is a matter of time and effort to be implemented in a more effective manner, and the mining sector is the one that is more prone to implement CSR practices in Peru, since they are already used to comply with international standards of social and environmental performance.
the Peruvian legal framework is not enough to establish and direct the CSR in the mining sector, but the European Union's legal framework is the right one.

the Peruvian mining sector, which is the most important in the country and one of the most important in Latin America, has not yet adopted CSR practices as part of its business strategy; there is no specific legal framework that regulates CSR practices; and the Peruvian government, through the Ministry of Energy and Mines, has been promoting CSR practices through a voluntary approach, but without the support of specific laws.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of law as a tool to promote and develop CSR.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the legal framework in place in Peru, specially in the mining sector, has not been able to promote CSR as a tool of social responsibility, but rather it is a legal framework that is not able to prevent the negative impact that the mining industry is generating.
the legal framework of CSR in the Peruvian mining sector is still in its infancy.

CSR in Peru mining sector is a legal requirement, and that the legal domain is the most appropriate way to achieve the development of CSR, but that there is still much to do in order to make CSR a reality in the mining industry.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CSR is not a new topic for the mining sector in Peru but the way of understanding it and the way of promoting it are new topics for the Peruvian mining sector.
the law is the most important tool in the development of CSR and the mining sector is one of the most important sectors in Peru.
CSR is not a legal requirement in Peru but a voluntary initiative, however the law is an important instrument to promote CSR in the country.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the legal framework in the mining sector in Peru has been designed to ensure the respect for human rights and the protection of the environment.
the Peruvian legal framework is not enough developed to promote CSR in mining sector.
the law is a powerful and necessary tool to promote and develop CSR in the mining sector in Peru.
